s: The wicked are opposed to the righteous: assigned the worst life and a long wounding. Their award reflects their actions and final state. As coadjutors of evil, they prepare its throne through lawless harm, remain in Evil Mind, and are harmed by Bountiful Spirit, receiving their portion far from Ahura Mazda’s love.

Heaven, the best mental state and world for the holy, contains the stars, moon, and sun. The better spirit wears its firm stones as a robe. After crossing the Kinvat Bridge, the holy enter it as the promised destination of glorified bodies.
Hell is the worst life for the wicked, opposed to Heaven and holiness; at life’s end, prescribed words may keep the soul away from it.
Life is opposed by its absence and threatened as spirits and demon-gods seek to pollute mortal lives through evil deeds.
Religions are presented as matters for individual decision. The hearers are urged to listen and choose rightly between them.

A clean, holy creation encompassing spiritual and mundane realms. In creation, two spirits complete separate deeds and choose separate realms, while Âramaiti gives bodies to spiritual creations of good and evil. The entire creation is included in sacrifice, linked to the beneficent ritual and benignant Religion, prayed for goodness and prosperity against evil creation, protected by the Praises of the Offering, and determines the world’s final order.

begins_with Daêvas [when they first seized the Demon of Wrath as their ally] The great struggle began when the Daêvas first seized the Demon of Wrath as their ally. Its eventual just vengeance will accompany the gaining of the Kingdom for Ahura.

makes world [progressive until perfection] The great renovation is the work of those who make the world progressive until perfection is reached. Those who bring it on are urged to be like the Ahuras of Mazda in helpful readiness.

Salvation is a universal blessing received by humankind when foretold punishment and blessing begin. Ahura Mazda teaches it in accordance with Asha, through Good Mind and inspired words. It belongs to those who choose the righteous way, maintain Righteousness, receive Ahura Mazda’s gifts, and worship the Fire in truth with prescribed ritual materials; it contrasts with the fate of followers of the Lie and the wicked.

The Lie is a harmful doctrinal power opposed to Righteousness, delivering its settlements to death. Followed by rejecters of truthful teaching, it is linked to evil rulers, wicked deeds, and the wicked’s eternal abode. Failing to oppose an evil wrongdoer leads there. Its demon, hate, and bondsmen are guarded against and prayed away, while the Kingdom is to smite it.

The cause of Righteousness is a cause of devotion to Ahura, associated with wisdom, salvation, Asha, Good Mind, good Religion, and Sovereign Power. It advances through declared doctrines and faithful truth, opposing the Lie as believers follow Ahura Mazda's order.

are_made_by the prophet [through preaching mighty truths] The living believers are urged to hear Ahura Mazda's truthful teaching, reject the sinner's command, and follow Righteous Order. They are to use the Good Mind in their words and actions and fulfill their vows with faith.
The two struggling bands receive deciding satisfaction through Ahura Mazda’s Spirit, Fire, and Righteousness, then live under his appointed ruler according to Righteousness.
Universal Weal and Immortality are lasting blessings given by Ahura Mazda through Righteous Order to faithful followers who follow His order.

l: the zealous and thrifty husbandman, Yasna
s: The husbandman is a holy, thrifty field toiler chosen by the Kine, endowed with Good Mind's wealth, helping and blessing through the good creed and Righteous Order.

does_not_share the good creed [because the Kine rejects him] The thieving nomad is rejected by the Kine's choice and shall not share the good creed. He is contrasted with the husbandman as one who does not receive the Kine's favor.

are_delivered_to_death_by Lie [through harmful doctrinal vows] The settlements of Righteousness are delivered to death by those who follow the doctrinal vows of the harmful Lie. Ahura Mazda created the holy settlements and revealed religious laws for them.
The enlightened man follows holy Faith, pursues Daêna in word and action, aligns will and wish with his creed, and receives Ahura Mazda’s best teachings through Righteous Order.

The evil-doer harms the pious husbandman’s herd and flock and aids the wicked by preparing evil’s throne; the unit asks what award he receives, contrasting him with promoters of Ahura Mazda’s holy Rule.

is_a chosen saint [of Ahura Mazda] The chosen saint receives Universal Weal and Immortality, along with whatever is best, through Ahura Mazda’s Bountiful Spirit. He is associated with Good Mind and receives support from the feeble man, while the wicked ruler’s pride may slight him.

The rival-monarch seeks sovereignty through others’ plotting, using false religion to destroy doctrine, pervert understanding, seize wealth, reject the Kine and Sun, attack the saint, and bring homes, villages, towns, and provinces to ruin and death.

Daêva-worshippers are a group questioned over whether they ever ruled as worthy kings. They support wrongdoing with the Karpan and Usig, give the Kine to Rapine, withhold tribal wealth from Ahura Mazda’s worshippers, and fail to bring waters to righteous fields.

Grehma is an evil leader who values Karpans above Righteousness, seeks a kingdom in Hell, and works through Kavis and schemes against Ahura Mazda, linked to destroyers of life and conquering the Kine.

The Karpans are a group aligned with Grehma, the Kavis, and those desiring the Demon of lies. Inspired by polluted drunken joy and angry zeal, they crush the faithful and bring woe, but Zarathustra will drive out their disciples.
The Kavis, established by Grehma to oppose Ahura Mazda, scheme deceptively for the wicked until Zarathustra drives out their disciples.

Immortality is Ahura Mazda’s abiding, saving, and greatest gift, given through holy deeds, words, and sacrifice. A blessing for the righteous and chosen saint, it is granted with Weal to those who heed His teaching, desired in eternal existence, and increased by Âramaiti with Universal Weal and the Righteous Order.

A settlement within Province, blessed as the source of Zaothras for a safe, quiet, joyful, long abode; every Mazdayasnian village likewise receives prayers for safety, joy, longevity, succour, salvation, and praise.

Sacrifice is offered with self-humbling praise and homage to Ahura Mazda, Righteousness, and guarded settlements. Through it, worshippers seek approach, rewards, and grace; Ahura Mazda receives it and grants requested gifts. Withholding sacrifice brings worse than evil, while the Immortals are asked to accept it.
Doctrines are destroyed, perverted, and declared by evil teachers and men, yet inherited as treasures delivered as Mazda’s word amid Zarathustra’s effort to establish Ahura Mazda’s precepts.
is_a unit of a longer document Yasna XXXIII. presents prayers, hopes, moral commitments, requests for divine guidance and power, and Zarathustra’s self-consecration.

Ratu is an allied peer of the master, dwelling in the work-field of the Righteous Order and pastures of Thy Good Mind. Ruling from Righteousness, Ratu creates mental goodness and actions for Mazda, and speaks a blessing for the good servant’s acquisition and reward.

Religious faith receives offerings through opposition to evil and through good deeds, thoughts, words, labour, and admonition for another’s good. The Zarathustrian Faith is described as Ahura's Religion, whose long enduring prominence is desired within the house.
is_dwelling_place_of Ahura Mazda The Realm of Good Mind is associated with long life and the manifestation of the Good Mind among the tribes.
are_manifest_among religious faith [manifold] Offerings of worship are to become manifest among the worshippers, and Zarathustra asks for zeal and help in making them so.

Righteous Order is Righteousness, the Holy Order within Mazda's Mãthra, and the Best. It is a righteous order and way, called the straightest path and the only way to obtain the Kine's welfare. Associated with Ahura Mazda, the Good Mind, Sovereign Power, the Bountiful Immortals, and ritual law, it provides shelter for worshippers and requires active fulfillment of its precepts toward clean and better creatures. It protects and saves the religious choice, guards and saves flocks and herds, enables the Kine to be possessed, grants wished-for boons and sacred reward, and brings grace, justice, prosperity, lands, settlements, victory, and approach to Ahura Mazda in worship. It may win back the disaffected and enables righteous action. The holy ritual has appointed times and seasons in which the Gâthas rule as leading chants. Though persecuted by those opposed through wicked thoughts, words, and works, it is invoked for encounter and overthrow of its persecutors. It culminates as the basis of the excellent Ratu's rule, prosperity to salvation, and the best life of the saints.

Weal is Ahura Mazda’s abiding, eternal gift: a saving power and blessing for the righteous, complete welfare in ritual order. It comes to those who obediently attend Ahura Mazda’s declared word, is established with Immortality, and is requested from the Yazads and Ahura Mazda for petitioners’ well-being.
Universal Weal, one of Ahura Mazda’s two greatest gifts, is increased by Âramaiti with Immortality and the Righteous Order, providing food and removing hatred and foes.

Fire is Ahura Mazda’s sacred, bounteous son and a powerful force of Righteous Order. Called the Fire of the Lord and bearing the most potent name for grace, it is an offering of praise and holiness, meet for sacrifice and worthy of homage. Received joyfully in a house, it helps settlements yet harms the hater as with weapons. It gives a good bestowal to the two striving throngs, accompanying Piety and Righteous moral Order, and grants Weal and Deathlessness. Fed as prescribed with wood, perfume, sacred butter, and placed andirons, it remains aflame in the house and furthers progress and heroic renovation until its completion. It gives glory, nourishment, booty, offspring, instructors, reward, and renown. Addressing those for whom it cooks night and morning meals, it keenly examines those who approach. It blesses the worshipper who brings properly prepared wood, Baresman, or Hadhânaêpata plant, extending blessing to kine and people, while receiving praises and seeking propitiation of the good waters as lofty lord of ritual.

Settlements are guarded by Good Mind, advanced by Mazda and victory, and urged to remain uncorrupted. Endangered by evil rulers, they thrive through mental goodness and Ahura Mazda’s favor; those who further Piety’s settlements with zeal receive Mazda’s presence and joyful grace, while offerings protect present and saving settlements.
Tyrants rule provinces with evil rule inspired by drunken joy; the account asks when their rule will end.

Saints are souls, men and women worshipped wherever born. With good consciences, they conquer the Daêvas, bring wicked converts in penitence, and receive the Realm through Good Mind. Unharmed by Ahura Mazda’s Bountiful Spirit, they are associated with wise perceptions, sacred blessings, guileless characteristics, and due recognition; their Fravashis aid better men.

are_heard_in Home-of-song [as offered by saints] Praises are offered to Ahura Mazda, the Righteous Order, and the Good Mind in sacrifice and worship. Stars, suns, and the Aurora are described as shining works that speak the praise of the Great Giver through the Righteous Order.

Worship is a service of homage and praise, chiefly offered to Ahura Mazda, with praises, eternal names, supplication, raised hands, sacred metric feet, and freely-giving service. It unfolds through wise, self-humbling devotion, drawing near to the eternal ones, and support from Good Mind. Its direction expands to Righteousness, the Gâthas, Praises of the Yasna, good waters, Fravashis and souls of saints, Immortals, Blessedness, and Sraosha, through recitation, chanting, and complete offering. Its results include Blessedness, Piety, well-thought thought, well-spoken word, and well-done deed; it protects settlements and persons and defends against Daêva and evil-minded man.
Paths through Righteousness, taught by Ahura Mazda and trodden by Good Mind within saints, connect religious precepts and Saviours’ laws, enabling the well-doer to thrive.

Sacred reward and blessing are given and appointed by Ahura Mazda for souls according to what is most meet for their deserving. Established by Ahura Mazda’s ordinance, they follow the Good Mind and Righteousness through its deeds, serving bodily life and extending to this world, the spiritual, and the life of mind with protecting guardianship.
Good actions, joined with good thoughts and words, are praised and chosen by worshippers as best for both worlds.
Prayer is offered by the praiser to Ahura Mazda with praises, seeking grace, protection, righteous lands, guidance, and help through supplication and stretched hands.

is_a Yasna Haptanghâiti Yasna XXXV. praises Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Righteousness, and the Mazdayasnian Faith. It calls for their worship, for good thoughts, words, and actions, and for the practice and diffusion of the faith.
Yasna Haptanghâiti is a supplement and portion of the Yasna: a prayer for practicing and spreading faith, offered as a brave, holy ritual chief, and used in worship of the Bountiful Immortals.

The Mazdayasnian Faith is a benignant, good, holy religion and religious choice. Its practice, teachings, and diffusion are prayerful purposes. Zarathustra seeks to establish and maintain it with Ahura Mazda's grace and the Good Mind, declaring its truths and advancing it through supporters. Proclaimed with the pure Daêna, it is guarded against Wrath of Rapine and joined by believing natures. Associated with wisdom, law, true life, Asha, and a great cause, it is received with desire and worshipped whole, opposed to the Daêvas.
Good thoughts, praised as best, join good words and actions; worshippers choose, honor, and implant them now and hereafter.
Good words are praised as best, chosen and proclaimed by worshippers with good thoughts and actions as Righteousness and better mind.

Yasna is a good religious sacrifice and an instrument of prayer, praise, worship, and homage offered to Ahura Mazda. It matters as the most legitimate Yasna: a whole collection of Praises, words, sacred metres, ending words, and Praise-songs, through which worshippers proclaim teachings, seek light and blessings, and approach Ahura Mazda and the Righteous Order. It begins with spoken offerings and worship of the Bountiful Immortals; its praises are remembered, recited, learned, taught, repeated, chanted, and offered. It culminates in worship of the entire collection, invoking waters, supporting settlements, and requesting prosperity to salvation.
Zeal is requested from the Fire of Ahura Mazda as a friendly gift. It supports the greatest undertaking among the efforts described in the unit.
is_a body of Ahura Mazda [most beauteous] The stars are identified as part of Ahura Mazda’s body. Deep acknowledgments are made to them.

Waters are a natural entity worshipped in rain, pools and vats, vessels, seas, earth, springs, streams, wells, canals, and running or standing forms. They are female Ahuras of Ahura, made by Ahura Mazda, Mazda-made, good, maternal, productive, full-flowing, beautiful, and useful for bathing. They nourish the frail and needy before birth, are mother of life, and can reach sickness and misfortune with long arms. Their sounding waves, flood and ebb, and roar mark their power. Worshippers offer them inculcated words and sanctified Zaothras, seeking their favour. The waters grant splendour, glory, health, vigour, possessions, legitimate offspring, long life, and the best life of the Saints to those who sacrifice piously. Yet they are also asked to withhold benefits from evildoers and to come destructively as torments against wicked men.
bears us The earth is worshipped as the one that bears those who worship, together with the wives of Ahura Mazda.

The Yazads are holy beings, bestowers of better gifts who abide beside Kine for protection and support. Mighty and powerful, they are asked to grant greater, more beautiful, and precious gifts, including Immortality and Welfare. As lords of the ritual order, they are worshipped and sacrificed to, including Apãm-napât and Nairya-sangha.

The Fravashis of the saints are good, heroic, bountiful spirits belonging to saints, holy men, and holy women. Desired from first to last, they are worshipped and sacrificed to across the bodily and mental worlds. Worshippers ask them to come to the house and accompany the sacrificer hand in hand. Their blessed gifts heal, further better men, hinder the hostile, and promote abundant riches and glory. Their reach is figured as extending earth, rivers, and the high-reaching sun. They include Fravashis of saints who live or have lived, are born or yet to be born, and those connected with houses, villages, districts, provinces, and the Zarathustrôtemas. They are invited to draw near and are said to have borne waters upstream.
is_a faith [good] Good Faith is worshipped as the good law of thrift.
Trained, tame, broken-in beasts are requested for pastures, riding, and bearing, providing companionship, enduring vigour, and rejoicing grace.
is_a men [righteous] Righteous men are requested from Ahura Mazda.

Bountiful Âramaiti is personified Piety, a bountiful and perfect virtue. She increases prosperity alongside righteous ritual and moral Truth, supports peace and pastures for the Kine, and teaches those who seek her. Linked with Ahura Mazda’s Bountiful Spirit and Fire, she is expected with Righteous Order to bring homes, relief from cruel people, and blessings. Though Bendva failed to sustain her, Âramaiti endures through self-humbling praise and sacrifice, approaches when asked, speaks her truths, and is associated with Kavi Vîstâspa.
is_with Ahura Mazda Fellowship with Ahura Mazda is requested as part of what may be attained in this world and the spiritual.

l: lovers and producers of the Right, Yasna
s: A group loves and produces the Right, with its members requested as righteous men.
The Right is associated with men who love and produce it.
A kinsman lord is requested for petitioners, together with village labourers and likewise clients or peers.
belongs_to village The labourers of the village are requested to be associated with a kinsman lord.
Clients or peers are requested to be present alongside the kinsman lord and the labourers of the village.

is_a prayer [to Ahura] Yasna XLI. praises and worships Ahura Mazda and Righteousness the Best. It asks for Ahura Mazda’s good Kingdom, long life, power, salvation, protection, and reward, and concludes with a sacrifice to Yasna Haptanghâiti.

l: people devoted to Ahura Mazda, Yasna
s: worships Ahura Mazda The worshippers of Ahura Mazda are associated with the Faith, Piety, Righteousness, and the Good Mind. The speaker asks how Piety may again approach them and how they may receive protection, guidance, and the blessings of Welfare and Immortality.

Ahura Mazda is a deity: the all-wise Lord, Creator, bountiful and most beneficent holy one. He made the stormy wind and is described as maker of the Kine, plants, waters, and all good things; he also causes plants to flourish for the Kine’s nurture. He possesses the Bountiful Spirit, wise intelligence, Good Mind, Righteous Order, Sovereign Power, and a sovereign realm. Through these powers he establishes and grants Weal, Welfare, Immortality, royal power, saving support, and prosperity, especially to his chosen saint and worshippers. He is father of Good Mind and Righteous moral Order, gives Âramaiti and Fire, and made the joy-creating Kine. He despises the Daêva-gods. Across the records, he is praised and sought through Righteousness, Good Mind, Piety, ritual offerings, and worship with the Bountiful Immortals and Sraosha. Worshippers ask him for protection, truth, strength, courage, good rule, victory, reward, blessing, healthy herds and settlements, and salvation. He shows Zarathustra how to pray and offer to the waters, and is asked to grant Immortality and Welfare through Good Mind in the doctrine. At the last ending of life, he promises to keep the soul away from Hell when prescribed words are pronounced.

is_high high Haraiti is described as high and lofty, with Sraosha’s house standing on its highest height. Haoma worshipped Sraosha there, and the house is described as self-lighted within and star-studded without.
Lands live in justice and display the sun’s splendours; sought and gained for the cause, they may include an imperilled farm made to flourish near foemen’s fields by a righteous heroic settler.
is_a sea Vouru-kasha contains the sea where the sacred Unicorn (?) stands. Sacrifice is offered to that sea.
Haoma, a golden-flowered healer growing on heights, is sacrificed to; it restores, advances this world, drives death afar, and worships Sraosha on high Haraiti.

have Saviours of the Provinces [as their saviours] The provinces are subject to tyrants' evil rule and are to receive Saviours. The Saviours will act for the provinces through the Good Mind, the Righteous Order, and Ahura Mazda's commandments.

Sraosha is Obedience, also described as listening or attentive Obedience, and Ahura Mazda’s messenger. He approaches Zarathustra with the Good Mind, questions him, and directs him toward the quiet, better mind’s teaching, while being asked to accompany him with holy recompense and spiritual splendour. Blessed, stately, holy, victorious, and devoted to Ahura Mazda, Sraosha is a ritual lord and chief: first to adore Ahura Mazda, first to worship the Bountiful Immortals, and first to chant Zarathustra’s five Gâthas. Present for worship and worshipped with sacrifice, he receives praises and aids holy creation. His central work is protection and conquest. He furthers and guards settlements, houses, people, Ahura Mazda’s creatures, and the corporeal world, keeping destructive terrors away and defending against unhappy death, Wrath, hostile hosts, and their assaults. Sleepless and vigilant, he battles the Daêvas day and night, slays them and the Lie-demon, smites Aêshema, and hews down Angra Mainyu, Rapine, and the Daêvas of Mazendran. A strong, persistent youth and mighty conqueror, he bears victory-making powers and weapons, including the Ahuna-vairya as an axe of victory and a battle-axe that cleaves Daêvas’ skulls. He travels from India in the East to the West, and by victorious power, wise conduct, and full knowledge causes the Bountiful Immortals to descend upon the earth. Within the sacrificer’s house, he governs and is asked to conquer disobedience.

Bountiful Spirit is Ahura Mazda’s most bounteous spirit. It brings blessedness through words and Âramaiti’s hands, grants sovereign power, gifts, spiritual glory, Universal Weal, and Immortality to chosen saints, blesses contending throngs with certainty and peace, and harms the wicked but not saints.
Ahura Mazda’s foremost servant hates Daêva-worshippers and repeatedly asks Ahura Mazda for truth about creation, righteousness, wickedness, and protection to increase in goodness.

Holy Faith is the best holy faith of Ahura Mazda's people, sought for hallowing and understanding. Taught by the beneficent kingdom's lord, it furthers Righteous Order, advances lands in Asha, and makes actions just. The enlightened man closely follows it, aligning will, creed, words, and actions.

The Demon-of-the-Lie is a rebellious, harmful demon opposed by Righteousness’s friends and inspiring the foes. She gives them no light; the speaker seeks her banishment, delivery to the Righteous Order, death through doctrine, destruction of her evil believers, and smiting through action in accordance with the Righteous Order.

is_a hymn Yasna XLV declares the Doctrine of Dualism and presents teachings concerning Ahura Mazda, the two first spirits, obedience, righteousness, and the consequences for the righteous and the wicked.

The wicked are miscreants of the Lie who scheme with evil will, support Wrath of Rapine and the Daêvas, and pervert Faith and Insight. They withhold sacrifice, reject the holy rule, and are associated with evil words and consciences. Abjured by the speaker, they receive worse than evil, punishment, evil food, and dwelling in the Lie’s abode. The righteous wound them with justice, and they are called forth for encounter and overthrow.
are_despised_by Ahura Mazda The Daêva-gods are described as having been despised, along with alien men, because they had held Ahura Mazda in derision.

Saoshyant is a saving prophet and Lord of saving power, associated with bounteous Faith. Described as friend, brother, or father, he is expected to see the Good Mind’s grace, receive recompense, and is worshiped as a victorious smiter.

is_a eternal gift Immortality is identified with Welfare as a gift greater, better, more beautiful, and more precious than the requested wealth and offspring. It is requested from the Yazads and from Ahura Mazda.
is_joined_with the hero (Gâmâspa's companion) [in the course of the holy Order and in the reward] Gâmâspa is joined with the “hero” in the best recompense and in the course of the Holy Order.

Kinvat Bridge is a bridge and place of judgment crossed by souls. Zarathustra leads the righteous there, and souls cross it in holiness after prescribed acts and speech. At the bridge, conscience crushes the wicked spirit; the wicked miss the path, fall into the Lie’s abode, and struggle to pollute Asha’s paths.

is_a lasting habitation [for the wicked] The abode of the Lie is the everlasting habitation of the Karpan and Kavi who join in governments to destroy human life with evil deeds. Those who miss the path at the Judge's Bridge fall there.

l: champion of the holy Order, Yasna
s: Champion of the holy Order, expected to smite an evil heretic and oppose Demon-of-the-Lie in a future good consummation.
The Wrath-demon of rapine, an evil power associated with Râma, is supported by schemers, opposed by the faithful, and cast down in the coming struggle.

belongs_to bounteous man [through a sacred bond] The refuge is to be held fast by those abiding by the Good Mind and the Righteous Order. The bounteous man belongs to its sacred bond, and Ahura Mazda's struggling saint is to be placed there in His world.

has potent prayer [as its means of coming] The holy Reign is sought through potent prayer, along with its sacred reward and blessing. The speaker asks how to seek helpers for spreading and maintaining it while living through the Good Spirit's deeds.
drive_away drunken joy [from the polluted soil] The men of mind's perfection are awaited as those who will drive away the polluted drunken joy that empowers the Karpans and supports tyrannical rule.
Saviours of the Provinces advance through Good Mind's grace and mental keenness, perform Ahura Mazda's commanded deeds under Holy Order, and steadfastly oppose hate.

are_led_by champion of the holy Order [as leader of the tribes] The conflicts are future struggles in which the speaker seeks strength and courage as leader of the tribes. They are associated with the hoped-for defeat of evil heretics, the Demon-of-the-Lie, rapine, envy, and oppressive rulers.

is_a religious text Yasna XLIX presents reverses and hopes, addressing Bendva’s opposition, appeals to Ahura Mazda, the roles of Frashaostra and other chiefs, and the fates of the faithful and wicked.

Bendva is a powerful, deceptive adversary with an evil judge, continually fighting the speaker and able to crush his strength; estranged from the Righteous Order, he neither maintains Piety nor seeks insight through Good Mind.

The Lie is an opposing creation to good rule, tied to miscreants, false teachings, and the Demon-of-the-Lie. It begins as an evil judge’s association and ends as the Home of the Lie, where Karpan doctrine delivers souls of evil men.
Bendva’s death is sought from Ahura Mazda through Good Mind as relief from the speaker’s sorrow and opposition.
A supplicant approaches Ahura Mazda with Yasnas, prayer, worship, sacrifice, and praises, seeking grace, protection, assistance, righteous lands, sacred privilege, success, and the Home-of-song.

is_a sacred power [of Ahura Mazda] The Sovereign Authority is associated with Ahura Mazda and with the gift granted through the Righteous Order. Its help enables the wisher to stand upon the certain pathway.

contains the speaker (the supplicant) [after death] The Home-of-song is the place where the speaker expects to hear the praises of offering saints who see Ahura Mazda’s face. The speaker seeks to reach it through worship and the certain pathway.
The Mãthra-word belongs to Ahura Mazda; cheered servants speak it, and its speaker leads people toward weal and bliss.

are_yoked_by the speaker (the supplicant) [for their course toward heaven] Mãthra-speakers are urged and yoked for their sacred course toward the Bridges where adoration is complete. They proclaim the righteous way and are joined with the Righteous Order and Good Mind for help.

Good Government of Ahura, a wished-for good, is chosen for bringing happiness and opposing oppressive actions through holy Order and pious zeal; the speaker seeks Ahura Mazda’s continual help to bring it about.

l: the Assembly of the Faithful, Yasna
s: assembles the faithful [to hear Ahura Mazda] The Assembly of the Faithful is addressed as the gathered people who hear Ahura Mazda and seek guidance. The speaker appeals to them concerning loyalty to Zarathustra, the good Religion, Asha, and the great cause.
Wealth, sought for waters, gives its holder power; Yasna LI requests it as prosperity granted and preserved under Sovereign Power, linked with Kine, herds, tillers, and Ahura Mazda’s blessings.

is_a prayer [for sanctity and its benefits] Yasna LII (Sp. LI) contains A Prayer for Sanctity and Its Benefits. It describes prayers for sanctity, prosperity, healing virtue, and protection from the Daêvas.

l: A Prayer for Sanctity and Its Benefits, Yasna
s: concerns sanctity [and its benefits] A Prayer for Sanctity and Its Benefits asks for goodness, benefits, and sanctity for present, emerging, and future generations. It also seeks prosperity for the holy creation and opposition to the entire evil creation.

Blessedness is a good Sanctity closely knit with Righteous Order. Prayed for as a source of prosperity and long-lasting shelter, it brings healing, gifts, blessings, and later success, perfects and incites us, opposes evil creation, and overwhelms the Daêvas’ harmful malice.
Benefits are requested for all holy and clean creation across generations, with greatest, best, and most beautiful benefits linked to sacrifice, homage, praise, and prosperity.
Prosperity is presented as accompanying sanctity and receiving shelter from it. The prayer seeks prosperity for the abode, the entire creation of the holy, and the clean.
Healing virtue comes in waters, belongs to cattle, is found in plants, and is borne by sanctity as a benefit.
The entire evil creation is opposed as the counterpart of the prosperity sought for the entire creation of the holy and the clean.
A Yasna within the Gâthas, presenting prayers, devotion, marriage counsel, protection from the Lie-demon, and sinners’ defeat.

is_founded_by Ahura Mazda The Faith of the Saoshyant is a faith that Ahura Mazda will found. Kavi Vîstâspa, Zarathustra Spitâma, and Frashaostra offer praise and Yasna confessions while making straight paths for it.

Pourukista, Zarathustra’s young daughter, is given Haêkat-aspid and Spitâmi as help in the Good Mind’s true service. She is counseled to act justly with them, loves and vies with Haêkat-aspid, and receives insight from his counsel.
Righteous women earn recompense, resist lustful desire, bring forth Saoshyant's champion, and triumph by naming Vayu as their last word.
Maidens are given monitions for marrying and urged to heed the laws of the Faith so that they may obtain the life of the Good Mind on earth and in heaven.

cherish_each_other Righteousness [for a happy home-life] Bride and bridegroom are instructed to cherish each other in Righteousness. Their mutual care is presented as the condition for a happy home-life.
Marriage counsel addresses maidens, bride, and bridegroom, urging faithful laws, mutual righteous cherishing, shared counsel with Ârmaiti’s mind, and just action.

is_happy happy [when bride and bridegroom cherish each other in Righteousness] Home-life is said to be happy when bride and bridegroom cherish each other in Righteousness. Peace is also sought for dwellings and hamlets.
A best answered prayer asks Ahura Mazda for good-Order boons, eternal prosperity, and deceivers’ conversion into good-Faith disciples.
is_a Yasna Yasna LIV (Sp. LIII) is titled The Airyemâ-Ishyô. It contains prayers for grace and sacred reward, and sacrifices to the Airyemâ-ishyô, the Gâthas, and the Praises of the Yasna.
A powerful, victoriously smiting holy ritual sentence, opposing assaulting malice, receiving sacrifice, and standing greatest in ritual order.
is_a desired friend and peers-man The Airyaman is described as the desired friend and peers-man. It is asked to draw near for grace to the men and women who are taught of Zarathustra.

The Praises of the Yasna are an entire collection and productions of the world of old, instituted in the world of yore. They are recollected and put in use, then learned and taught in the present ritual tradition. Worship unfolds through holding them in mind, repeating, remembering, reciting, chanting, and complete offering, which furthers the world through grace. Their careful language has reached its object; worshippers sacrifice to the collection and offer homage to beautiful forms of Ahura Mazda, the stars, and the highest of the high.
A Yasna unit concludes worship of the Gâthas and begins worship of the Staota Yêsnya.
The Staota Yêsnya is identified as beginning in this unit.

Yasna LV presents riches, consciousness, soul, and selves as offerings to the Gâthas, alongside worship of divine Righteousness, Good Mind, and the Praises of the Yasna through recitation, memorised recital, chanting, and offering.

l: Gâthas as guardians and spiritual food, Yasna
s: The Gâthas are guardians and defenders, spiritual food and clothing for souls, and just, righteous, abundant givers of rewards for the world beyond the present.

l: religious order of the settlements, Yasna
s: is_protected_by Praises of the Offering [together with the settlements that are now being furthered and those that shall bring salvation] The religious order of the settlements is to be protected and guarded by the victorious and beneficent effects associated with the Gâthas and the Praises of the Offering.

Praises of the Offering is an offering to the bountiful Gâthas, produced by Mazda as most beneficent. It is invoked to appear with power, victory, health, healing, progress, growth, preparation, protection, beneficence, sanctity, and gifts for those who understand.

is_a offering [good] The offering consists of all landed riches and the persons, bodies, consciousness, souls, and Fravashi of those presenting it. The Praises of the Yasna are also worshipped in their complete offering.
is_an_introduction_to Srôsh Yast Yasna LVI (Sp. LV) introduces the Srôsh Yast and contains invocations of Sraosha for worship.
The Srôsh Yast, a Yast titled Yasna LVII, presents praises, worship, and petitions directed to Sraosha.

is_a Yasna Yasna LVII (Sp. LVI) is presented as a unit of worship and praise for Sraosha, or Obedience the blessed. It describes his victories, guardianship, ritual authority, and protection of people and settlements.
Angra Mainyu, a wicked evil being, has evil creatures and is filled with death; his encounter and displacement are sought.

Mazdayasnians are worshippers who offer sacrifice with colleagues, disciples, men, women, children, and maidens, asking for desire and knowledge of the straightest path, defeat of oppression and malice, and the saints’ best life.
Baresman is sacrificed to with Zaothra and girdle, its band, and is spread with sanctity.
A prayer pealed forth in liturgy between heaven and earth.

is_a by-spoken The Fshûshô-Mãthra describes worship as a shelter from the Daêva and the evil-minded man. It praises the owner of herds, asks for salvation and protection, and offers thoughts, words, actions, herds, and men to the Bountiful Spirit.

is_a Yasna Yasna LVIII (Sp. LVII) is identified as The Fshûshô-Mãthra. It presents worship as protection, entrusts settlements and persons to its care, and offers praise to Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, the Fire of Ahura Mazda, and the Praises of the Yasna.

The owner of herds is called righteous, victorious when he strikes, and best. He is father of the Kine, the holy man, and sanctified creation; bestows blessings in verity; and watches over worship together with the Righteous Order.
Yasna LIX, “Mutual Blessings,” unfolds through worship and spoken blessings to concluding praises.
“Mutual Blessings” is the title of this unit. The Ratu gives a blessing to the Zaotar, and the Zaotar returns a blessing.
is_a victorious blow [Ahura-made] Verethraghna is worshiped as the Ahura-made, victorious blow.

Zaothra is a sanctified ceremonial offering for propitiation. Offered to the Ahurian One, it unfolds with Haoma, flesh, milk, and Hadhânaêpata lifted with sacred regularity, then is invoked for health, healing, progress, growth, merit, renown, equanimity, and victory.

obtains reward [far advanced in his good thoughts, and words, and deeds] The Zaotar is described as far advanced in good thoughts, words, and deeds. The Zaotar receives the Ratu’s blessing and responds by wishing what is better than the good and rejecting what is worse than the evil.
is_a excellent Ahû is described as excellent in the formula beginning, “As our Ahû is excellent.”

Asha Vahista, the most beautiful Bountiful Immortal and Righteousness the Best, is worshiped, asked to accompany worshippers approaching Ahura Mazda, then sent forth in prayer between heaven and earth.

is_a prayers for the dwelling of the sacrificer Yasna LX (Sp. LIX) is a prayer for the dwelling of the sacrificer. It invokes blessings, protection, prosperity, righteous order, and eventual attainment of Heaven.

A house receives sacred blessings, wise perceptions, righteous order, divine sovereignty, welfare, holy strength, and saints’ Fravashis. It has enduring glory, abundance, offspring, and companionship, while obedience, peace, generosity, reverence, and truthful speech prevail within it.

l: best world of the saints, Yasna
s: A shining, glorious Heaven devoted to Ahura Mazda, where glorified bodies reach the saints’ best world with Asha Vahista.
is_sent_forth prayer [in liturgy] YêNhê hâtãm is to be sent forth in the liturgy between heaven and earth.

l: good and pious Prayer for blessings, Yasna
s: Prayer, pious and good, is sent between heaven and earth in liturgies for blessings and to encounter and displace evil powers and beings.
Encounter is sought with Angra Mainyu, Kahvaredha, Kayadhas, and other evil or hostile beings.
Displacement is sought against Angra Mainyu and his creatures, including Kahvaredha and Kayadhas.
An evil being with male and female individual Kahvaredhas, named as targets for encounter and dislodgment.
Kayadhas are evil beings, including individual male and female Kayadhians, targeted for encounter and dislodgment.
is_a wicked The murderers of the saints are named as targets for encounter and overthrow.
are_not_congenial_to wicked [in their thoughts, words, and works] The holy ritual laws are the standard against which the thoughts, words, and works of the wicked are judged.

l: prophets who are yet to serve and save thy people, Yasna
s: Prophets yet to serve and save thy people will drive away the powerless Demon of the Lie, gaining power over her.
is_for dislodgment [entire] The entire evil world is to be dislodged.
Overthrow is sought against murderers of the saints, persecutors, the tyrant full of death, and the wicked.
Dislodgment is sought against Kahvaredha, Kayadhas, the Demon of the Lie, and the entire evil world.

l: man who worships the Fire, Yasna
s: A man worships the Fire in verity and truth, approaching with wood, Baresman, flesh, and a mortar; by bringing properly prepared sacred materials, he receives the Fire’s blessing and promised salvation.

is_brought Fire [well dried, sought out for flaming, and purified with the earnest blessing of the sacred ritual truth] Wood is to feed the Fire according to prescription. The Fire blesses the person who brings wood that is well dried, sought out for flaming, and purified with the earnest blessing of the sacred ritual truth.
The Fire is asked to remain aflame, shining, and growing in the house for the furtherance of the heroic renovation and until the good heroic time when the renovation has become complete.

The requested offspring is legitimate, sure-footed, wakeful, nurturing, orderly, influential, powerful, skilled, self-dependent, and able to redeem others from oppression. It is sought for the waters and will bless multitudes, advances the speaker’s line, Vîs, Zantu, and province, and delivers firm, righteous orders as rulers.
A Yasna praising Ardvi Sûra Anâhita and the waters, describing their powers and courses, then offering prayers for wealth, offspring, Immortality, and Welfare.

Ardvi Sûra Anâhita is wide-flowing water, healing, efficacious against Daêvas, devoted to Ahura Mazda’s lore, and worshipped with sacrifice in the corporeal world. She furthers living things, increases herds, settlements, and wealth, and helps the Province progress. She purifies men’s seed, women’s wombs and milk; sanctifies wombs for birth; aids women in labour; and brings timely milk. Sounding from afar and equal in bulk to all earthly waters, she flows with mighty volume from Hukairya to Vouru-kasha, through a thousand tributaries and outlets. Her chief outlet reaches the seven Karshvars, bearing waters to them in every season.

is_addressed_to Ahurian One Yasna LXVI (Sp. LXV) presents an offering addressed to the Ahurian One and made for the propitiation of Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Sraosha (Obedience) the blessed, and the Fire of Ahura Mazda.
The Ahurian One is addressed as the recipient of the Zaothra, which is offered with sanctity together with the Haoma and the flesh.
Propitiation is the offering’s purpose, seeking Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, blessed Sraosha (Obedience), and the Fire of Ahura Mazda.
Yasna LXVII (Sp. LXVI) is a text whose sections 1–4 parallel Y. XXIII with one phrase replaced and refer to Y. VII, while sections 5–7 refer to Y. XXXVIII.

A daughter of Ahura, the Ahurian One receives offerings and Yasna, is worshipped through sacrifice and good thought, and is asked for presence, protection, healing, prosperity, offspring, assistance, and heaven.
Zarathustra’s Fravashi is a spirit belonging to the saint and included among those offered sacrifice.
A chapter composed of fragments, referring to Y. XV, 2 and Y. LI, 1 and 22.

Institutions of religion are declared established, exact, and undeviating. They encompass Ahura Mazda’s associated powers and beings, including Good Mind, Righteousness, the desired Realm, Piety, Weal, Immortality, the Kine, Fire, Sraosha, Rashnu, Mithra, and Wind. They culminate in the good Mazdayasnian Religion and good, pious prayers for blessings and against belying and unbelieving words.
is_a The Yasna Concluding Yasna LXXI is the Yasna Concluding and presents the completed recital of the rites and the delivery of the Gâthas.
Mazda’s words are sacrificed to as fatal to evil thoughts, words, and deeds; they designate and cut down evil while invoking strength, victory, glory, and speed.

l: evil thought, word, and deed, Yasna
s: The evil thought, word, and deed are designated and then cut down and felled by the words which Mazda spake.
Soul, belonging to Zarathustra and protected from Hell by Ahura Mazda and prescribed final words, crosses the Kinvat Bridge in holiness to Heaven.
refers_to Y. LXI YASNA LXXII is identified as a unit and directs the reader to see YASNA LXI.

This document is a sequence of Visparad ritual units centered on Yasna offerings, praise, worship, and correctly performed sacred speech. It opens with offerings to the lords of all parts of creation, spiritual, earthly, aquatic, animal, seasonal, and ritual, and repeatedly joins Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Zarathustra Spitâma, the Gâthas, the Yasna Haptanghâiti, Haoma, Zaothra, Baresman, Fire, the Kine, waters, lands, plants, and holy communities within one ritual order. Visparad III formally begins the Haoma Offering through the Zaotar’s roll-call of ritual officers and community members, with the Ratu affirming their duties. Subsequent units present the speaker as priest, invoker, reciter, chanter, and confessor, offering body, life, ritual implements, prayers, sacred words, pressed Haomas, and praise. The text stresses exact memorising, chanting, recital, and offerings made without addition or omission, especially for the Gâthas and Yasna Haptanghâiti. It invokes numerous holy beings and principles, including Sraosha, Ashi, Âramaiti, Rashnu, Mithra, Fravashis, and Asha Vahista, and seeks blessing, righteousness, wisdom, health, fertility, protection, victory, salvation, and the advancement of settlements, houses, herds, and communities. Ethical instruction appears in the call to pursue good thoughts, words, and deeds, lawful conduct, husbandry, generosity to the needy, and Righteousness, while rejecting evil and unlawful acts. The later sections broaden worship to saints past, present, and future, the holy and clean creation, Heaven and the Best World, and the path toward them. The work closes by linking memorised good thoughts, words, and deeds, the Ahuna-vairya, and Airyemâ-ishyô with reward, healing, growth, victory, and the best approach to Heaven.
translated_by L.H. Mills Visparad I contains announcements and completions of Yasna offerings to various holy lords, festivals, chants, beings, places, and ritual observances.

The Yasna is a praise, announced, celebrated, and completed for holy subjects, named divine beings, seasonal and yearly festivals, ritual chants, and the Yasna Haptanghâiti. Taken up earnestly for waters, fruit-trees, saints, Kine, Gaya, Mãthra Spenta, Ahura Mazda, Zarathustra, and the Bountiful Immortals, it proceeds through its offering, chapters, metrical lines, words, and word-structure.

Ritual Order is holy, spiritual, and blessed. Its holy lords encompass creatures, festivals, seasons, chants, Gâthas, beings, places, and ritual powers, approached with praise and linked to spiritual and earthly authority. It is associated with Ahura Mazda, the Gâtha Ahunavaiti’s own ritual order, and the Ahuna-vairya as holy lord.
Yearly festivals, holy lords of ritual order, include Maidhyô-zaremaya through Hamaspathmaêdhaya.

Ahuna-vairya is a heard, memorised recital recited as a chant and offered wisely with sanctity. It carries many teachings of religious wisdom, is praised and approached, and is worshipped as holy lord of the ritual order, with Ahû and Ratu as constituent titles. As part of the Gâtha Ahunavaiti, it has chapters, metrical lines, words, and word-structure. It culminates as one of two means through which victory and other benefits are found through recital of good thoughts, words, and deeds.

Righteous Order is Righteousness the Best: a lauded being among the greatest, best, and most beautiful. Approached in praise, it underlies sacrifice and homage, provides growth for ritual deeds, and brings blessing and weal. It is connected with Âramaiti’s laws and holy creatures whose first quality is Righteousness, and is worshipped as Asha Vahista and the best wish.

Gâtha Ahunavaiti is a holy Gâtha, ruling in ritual order. Announced and completed as holy, it is mentioned with women who bring forth many sons of many talents and with a chant whose Ahû and Ratu come before it in the Yasna. It is approached with praise, alongside a chant having Alva and Ratu. It is then worshipped and sacrificed to in all its forms: measures, word-structure, Zand, questions, counter-questions, words, metric feet, chapters, recitals, and offerings. It is actively recited and used in worship, possessing wisdom, clearness, loving intention, sovereignty, ritual order, and an acquired boon.

Yasna Haptanghâiti is a holy, heroic Yasna, ruling in the ritual order and associated with the water Ardvi Anâhita. It has chapters, metred lines, words, and word-structure. It is to be pondered, attended to with devotion, memorised, and recited exactly, victoriously, and holily, free of harmful malice. It inculcates good thoughts, words, and deeds. Identified with the later Yasna, it becomes holy ritual chief as it recurs.
is_a holy ruler in the ritual order Ardvi Sûra Anâhita is approached in praise as holy and ruling in the ritual order.
A Gâtha, holy and ruling in ritual order, is announced, completed, and praised, addressed with brilliant Mazda-made mountains, then approached again with praise.
A Gâtha and holy lord ruling the ritual order, announced and completed as holy, then approached with praise beside holy mountains and Verethraghna.
Verethraghna is the Mazda-given, holy blow of victory and lord of ritual order, approached with praise; it furthers settlements and is associated with Victorious Ascendency.
A Gâtha, holy and ruling in ritual order, is announced, completed, and praised alongside Mithra of the wide pastures and Râman Hvâstra, unfolding through ritual address and approach.
Mithra, a holy lord of ritual order with wide pastures, is approached with praise alongside sacred entities.
A holy Gâtha ruling in ritual order, celebrated and completed after offerings, then approached with praise alongside Mithra, Râman Hvâstra, and other sacred entities.

l: good and pious Prayer for blessings, Visparad
s: A good, pious prayer for blessings and benediction, associated with offered Haomas and Zaothras. Included in ritual praise and celebration, it is uttered at a fitting moment, following the order of prayers and linked to victory, sanctification, and souls’ well-being.

Airyemâ-ishyô is a holy lord of the ritual order, praised with the Fshûshô-mãthra and Hadhaokhdha; as one of two, memorised recital of good thoughts, words, and deeds brings victory and other benefits.
Ahura is associated with questions asked of Ahura and with the lore of Ahura. The text also names the Ahurian Dahvyuma and the Ahurian Zarathustrôtema as holy lords of the ritual order.
is_a lords of the ritual order [Ahurian; holy] The remedies of the Zarathustrôtema accompany certain offered Haomas and Zaothras.
Kine are blessed cattle: confession is made for them, their body receives homage and praise, and speakers address supplications to them through chant and ceremonial actions.
is_a ritual offering The speaker performs this Zaothra while approaching and praising numerous lords, festivals, Gâthas, divine beings, people, and places.
Baresman is a holy ritual chief and implement with Zaothra and a girdle, spread with sanctity, used with Zaothra as the speaker approaches and praises entities.

is_a Yearly festivals [holy] The holy Yearly festivals are approached with praise as lords of the ritual order, including Maidhyô-zaremaya, Maidhyô-shema, Paitishahya, Ayâthrima, Maidhyâirya, and Hamaspathmaêdhaya.
Settlements are praised as having a future and are advanced in righteous order by ritual, holy goodness, and maintaining the Mãthra of the Saoshyant.

Ahura Mazda is a holy spiritual lord and regulator of the spiritual creatures, repeatedly addressed as Lord, holy Lord of the ritual order, most helpful, bountiful, and best. He is central to worship, sacrifice, homage, and Yasna: he is approached with praise, summoned with the proper word, confessed as believed in, and given earnest homage, Haomas, offerings, celebrations, and sacred objects. He mentioned ritual chieftains to Zarathustra because of Asha Vahista and revealed lore in response to a question. Fire is identified as his son and his Fire is invoked, served with victorious words, and associated with his direction of the Avesta. His Garô Nmâna is worshipped as Heaven. He is said to have delivered ritual deeds and teachings, bears the titles Ahû and Ratu, and gives an acquired boon for promoting piety. Across the records, praise and invocation develop into offerings, ritual service, repeated worship, and final worship as the best.

Zarathustra Spitâma is a holy terrestrial lord and regulator of terrestrial creation, a saint, and an especially prominent possessor of the Mãthra. The speaker follows his order as a Mazdayasnian, and he directed how the Avesta should be said. Offerings, remedies, libations, sacrifice, Yasna, and homage are associated with him; his Fravashi and Blessedness are worshipped. He is honored as the living chief and master of those whose service Ahura Mazda has known as better, ending with earnest Yasna and homage.
A pious, holy man and saint is worshipped with the usta, along with his weal and salvation.
A text beginning the Haoma Offering by presenting the priest’s roll-call.
The Haoma Offering begins with the Zaotar’s summons and the roll-call of the priest.
Zaotar is a priest and Ratu’s announcer who calls priests, community, chiefs, immortals, and Saoshyants, identifies himself, and recites Staota Yêsnya with praise.
Ratu is a holy, learned priest who speaks from righteousness and answers the Zaotar’s calls by coming or fulfilling assigned priestly duties.

l: youth of holy thoughts, words and works, Visparad
s: A youth of holy thoughts, words and works, marked by good conscience and good speech, is summoned and described as given in marriage to his kin.
has wives of Ahura [wives] Ahura is addressed when the Zaotar summons His wives and describes a woman as being like the bounteous Âramaiti.
Âramaiti is a holy, good and bountiful being and ready mind, worshipped with bountiful creatures; her wisdom is associated with the laws of the Righteous Order.

Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians are a group whose chiefs are summoned with Fire-priests, warriors, and diligent husbandmen of the Mazdayasnian Faith. They celebrate sacrificial worship, homage, propitiation, and praise of the entire holy and clean creation at the sacrificial time for the Myazda-offering and at Ratufrîti. Steadfast in worship, they appear with wood-billets, perfumes, and supplicated blessings, while mortars are asked to become full of wisest teaching for them. They are then instructed to ready their feet, hands, and understandings for lawful deeds and avoidance of evil, further husbandry through good deeds, and render the needy rich.

Bountiful Immortals are holy, good, powerful Yazads, also called Amesha Spenta, who rule and dispose of all aright. They are ever-living, ever-helpful, bountiful bestowers of good, named with beauty, and dwell with or arise from Good Mind. Across Visparad, they are summoned by the Zaotar, invoked with Ahura Mazda, and addressed as recipients of sacrifice, homage, propitiation, praise, offerings, preparation, Haomas, and celebrations. They are worshipped according to ritual, with the usta and the saying the Spenta, alongside the shining sun; a chant is performed for them, and they are worshipped as the best.

Saoshyants are holy prophets of the provinces, summoned for help and praised as truthful, zealous, glorious, great, and powerful. They are connected with preparation, timely prayer for blessings, sanctification, victory over foes, and benefit to souls. Speakers identify themselves as Saoshyants of the provinces and of the house. In the end, holy Saoshyants are said to serve the speakers, who perform a chant for them.

The Mazdayasnian Faith follows Zarathustra and joins Fire-priests, warriors, and diligent husbandmen. It is linked with good Justice that advances settlements, with offered Haomas and Zaothras, and with religious practice through praises, Yasnas, doctrines, recitations, and movements.
The Zaotar declares that he will recite the Staota Yêsnya with memorised intoning, chanting, and praise.

l: holy thoughts, words and works, Visparad
s: is_a holy disposition Holy thoughts, words and works are associated with the summoned youth, woman, and holy man. The woman is advanced in them, and the holy man is advanced in his good thoughts, words, and deeds.
is_made_for Kine Confession is to be made for the Kine.
is_a offering [Myazda] The Myazda-offering has a sacrificial time at which Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians celebrate.
is_a prayer for blessings The Ratufrîti is a time at which Zarathustrian Mazdayasnians celebrate, and it is associated with the prayer for blessings.

Homage is a ritual offering or desire directed toward the entire holy creation and its sacred powers and beings. It is associated with sacrifice, propitiation, glorification, and adoration. In celebrations, it is offered to Ahura Mazda, divine beings, Fravashis, waters, trees, Kine, Mãthra Spenta, Zarathustra, and the Bountiful Immortals, through the Avesta and ritual prescripts.

is_for entire creation of the holy [with sacrifice, homage, and adoration] Propitiation is included among the purposes of the offerings and celebrations. It is directed toward Ahura Mazda, the Bountiful Immortals, Fravashis, and the entire creation of the holy and clean.

l: praise of the entire creation of the holy (and the clean), Visparad
s: is_a praise [of the entire creation of the holy (and the clean)] Praise of the entire creation of the holy (and the clean) is included among the acts performed at the sacrificial time.

A praiser priest, invoker, memoriser, reciter, and chanter who performs ritual for the Bountiful Immortals. The speaker chants sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise, offers body and life’s blessings, and confesses belief in Ahura Mazda.
Ritual prescribes worship of Ahura Mazda and Bountiful Immortals, with sacrifices to sacred words, Zarathustra, saints’ blessings, and hail.

Sacrifice is an offering and celebration for Ahura Mazda, divine beings, Fravashis, the Bountiful Immortals, Mãthra Spenta, the Mazdayasnian Religion, Yasnas, ritual lords, prayers, blessedness, and the entire holy, clean creation. It unfolds through homage, propitiation, praise, glorification, and adoration.
The speaker confesses his belief in Ahura Mazda as part of being a Mazdayasnian of the order of Zarathustra and in accordance with the Faith.

Visparad VI (Sp. VII) calls the good Amesha Spenta by their names of beauty and worships the Bountiful Immortals by their beautiful names. It acts with praise, the joyful reception of grace, intelligently offered Zaothras, and correctly spoken sacrificial words.
Righteousness the good is a good that provides a longing blessing in ritual observance.

Sraosha is Obedience, called blessed and worshipped. He receives announcement, presentation, sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and praise in celebrations. He accompanies the abundance of offerings with sanctity and is summoned with energetic effort to aid worship. Finally, he is called to worship Ahura Mazda, serve and ponder the Yasna Haptanghâiti, and carry out its devotion, memorisation, victorious holy recital, and victory.
Ashi is worshipped as good and blessed, embodying the blest order of rites and recompense.

The Fravashis of the saints are worshipped with announcement, sacrifice, homage, propitiation, praise, and earnest Yasna. They encompass the dead, living, unborn, and prophets who will serve and bring renovation, and are honored collectively and individually within and outside the Province.
is_a Heaven The Garô Nmâna of Ahura is worshipped as Heaven, the best world of the saints, shining and all glorious.

Heaven is the bright, all-glorious best world belonging to the saints. It is identified with the Garô Nmâna of Ahura and worshipped as an ancient, first-made earthly object. The records end by naming the best approach that leads to Heaven.
The Best World is described as the destination of a better path that is worshipped.
Arstât is good Justice, identified with Mazdayasnian Faith, worshipped for helping settlements advance and flourish.
Ancient institutions are worshipped as holy creations formed before sky, water, land, plants, and the Kine of blessed gift.

l: entire creation of the holy, Visparad
s: is_a entire creation [holy and clean] The entire creation of the holy is the object of sacrifice, homage, propitiation, and glorification.
The sea Vouru-kasha is worshipped.
Mazda is associated with the making of the stormy wind and Sleep. Sleep made by Mazda gladdens the herd and men. The remedies of Mazda accompany certain offered Haomas and Zaothras.

Fire is worshipped as Ahura Mazda's son and the holy lord of ritual order. The Yasna Haptanghâiti is recited for victorious words for Ahura Mazda's Fire; Yazads and Rashnus are said to have fire's seed.
The Kingdom is to belong to Him who rules the best.
Visparad IX concerns homage, praise, sacrifice, and propitiation directed toward sacred beings, virtues, practices, and the entire creation of the holy.

Haomas and Zaothras are offerings: pungent, bounteous, holy, victorious smiters, and foes of hatred. Offered with sanctity for a blessing, they are celebrated now and in the future, being pressed with sanctity and yet to be pressed. They accompany healing virtues, Kisti, Mazda, Zarathustra, Zarathustrôtema, disciples and itinerants versed in good devices, Faith, Prayer, veracity, and the word against unbelief.

is_a religious knowledge Kisti is identified with religious knowledge and is associated with the remedies of Mazda, Zarathustra, and the Zarathustrôtema. It is also honored together with the Priority for the powerful Ascendency.
